story.what_it_does: Colgate-Palmolive India sells oral care products and is known for brands like Colgate. It earned revenue from operations of ₹6,03,504 lakhs in FY2025-26, roughly flat on the prior year, and also reports export earnings of ₹278.11 crore.
story.plans: Management says it will keep stepping up advertising and drive growth ahead of profitability, with no EBITDA margin target. It also aims for premium products to exceed 50% of the business, with no date given, and has set 2030 plastic and 2040 net zero goals.
story.moat: Margins are high: gross margin was 69.6% and EBITDA margin 32.2% in Q4 FY26, with return on capital employed of 121% for FY26. Management also points to a rising premium contribution (up 35% over two years), though the notes give no explicit description of competitive advantages.

scenarios.story: Double-digit sales growth continues (12% in Q1 FY27 and 12.2% in Q2 FY27) and higher advertising and premium products build lasting demand. Gross margin stays near 69.6%, which supports profits.
signals_to_watch: Revenue growth staying near or above 12% year on year in coming quarters
Premium share of business moving toward the 50% target

scenarios.story: Sales keep growing well, but heavy advertising (16% of sales in Q1 FY27) holds profit growth below sales growth. Commodity inflation and GST effects continue to add noise.
signals_to_watch: Reported profit after tax versus the Rs 342 crore in Q2 FY27
Advertising spend as a share of sales after the 16% level in Q1 FY27

scenarios.story: Competition and cost inflation squeeze profits while advertising stays high, so adjusted profit growth stays weak (5.5% in Q2 FY27). Tax and port trust disputes could also lead to costs.
signals_to_watch: Adjusted profit growth excluding one-offs staying near 5.5% or lower
Outcomes of the Bombay Port Trust demand of ₹13,914 lakhs and the income tax appeal in the High Court
